proved_new_results.statement: Exact relative product identity for same-endpoint inverse branches; first order reversal forces cumulative exponent-sum order reversal.
Least-red prefix slack dominates log physical height. Tail-larger entry gap 2m forces sigma_(k-1)>2m and a length-sensitive exponent-1 density debt.
First tail-larger down-crossing at H=qL+r requires s >= q(beta_R L-A)+(beta_R r-E_r^-), giving a finite-turn phase bound for fixed cycle/slack.
In k=0, xi(c_j)=R#+1 exactly on the initial neutral spine; every off-spine cycle phase has xi(c_j)>=R#+3.

For k=0 with s=v2(R#+1)<L, the first post-neutral exit t=v2(3^s q-1) has next valuation r=v3(2^t-1) and must satisfy 2^(t+s-r)<3^(s-r). For s=2,3,4 the exit exponent is 2. Boundary s=L reduces to a separate one-plateau Diophantine equation.
Every exponent-1 plateau compresses exactly to invariant n=v2(y+1)+v3(y+1), 6-adic unit q, and xi level W=2^n q; its non-1 exit is determined by t=v2(3^n q-1).

For regular plateau exits t<n, a low threshold forces xi level increase and any xi descent requires the opposite high threshold. A k=0 cycle with s<L therefore needs a later high/deep exit after the low root exit.

Exact plateau xi-ratio telescoping reproduces A-L log2(3)=sum epsilon_j, so scalar plateau summation is equivalent to the classical cycle-product slope and discrete valuation transitions are the genuinely new content.

failed_route.statement: The first neutral-spine exit filter alone cannot close k=0; its inverse-limit conditional 2-adic survivor measure is about 0.5402990693.
